Map recorded cue labels to canonical cue pairs

Source: R/fba-cues.R
fba_cues_map.Rd

The experiment records the cues of each trial as one string, cues, made by concatenating the cue labels in the order they were shown, left to right. This function returns the table that turns that string into the canonical pair cue1, cue2, plus cues_reversed variable, which records whether the pair was shown in the reverse of its canonical order.

Usage

fba_cues_map(design = "three-stage-replication")

Arguments

design

Character(1). A recognised study design, as stored in provenance(x)$design.

Value

A tibble with columns label, cue1, cue2 and cues_reversed, containing one row per single cue and two rows per cue pair, one for each counterbalancing order.

Details

The table is derived from the cue sets defined by the design in the internal .catlas_design_specs list.

The canonicalisation invariant

cue1 and cue2 are always in the canonical order the design defines, whichever side of the screen each cue appeared on. "DQ" and "QD" both resolve to cue1 = "D", cue2 = "Q", with only cues_reversed telling them apart. Any join on c("cue1", "cue2") therefore matches both presentation orders. Single-cue trials have cue2 = NA and cues_reversed = NA.

Examples

fba_cues_map("three-stage-replication")
#> # A tibble: 56 × 4
#>    label cue1  cue2  cues_reversed
#>    <chr> <chr> <chr> <lgl>        
#>  1 A     A     NA    NA           
#>  2 C     C     NA    NA           
#>  3 E     E     NA    NA           
#>  4 G     G     NA    NA           
#>  5 I     I     NA    NA           
#>  6 L     L     NA    NA           
#>  7 O     O     NA    NA           
#>  8 R     R     NA    NA           
#>  9 AB    A     B     FALSE        
#> 10 BA    A     B     TRUE         
#> # ℹ 46 more rows
